analysis.title: CIO View: Bonds
key_insights: UBS CIO keeps an Attractive recommendation on the bond asset class, with Attractive views on high grade, investment grade, emerging market and high yield.

After a sharp rise in benchmark yields through September and a reversal in October and November, UBS sees bond markets finding an equilibrium, even though realized inflation is elevated and surprised to the upside again in the US.

Energy prices have fallen materially since the midterm elections, lowering market-based inflation expectations. Tighter financial conditions are becoming a constraint on how high yields can rise, most visibly in the Eurozone, where long-dated yields featured in the ECB's October decision to hold rates.

Starting yields are the main driver of forward returns. It would take a rise of well over 100bp in 5-year yields for capital losses to offset a year of income. UBS views such a move as unlikely because policymakers would respond.

UBS expects near-term yield stability and then a gradual move to lower yields next year. It favors short to medium maturities strategically, and says extending toward the 10-year area in quality issuers suits tactical investors or those seeking diversification.

AI capex sentiment is a source of market volatility. Credit spreads of several neocloud issuers that debt-finance chips and data centers have repriced sharply, mostly in high yield, loans and private markets. UBS frames it as a cost of capital and return on investment debate, with compute demand still robust.

Large technology companies that fund more capex with debt now trade at spreads implying multi-notch downgrades. Off-balance-sheet projects not yet online carry no operating-lease accounting, and UBS thinks the market may be assigning excessive premia given the lack of transparency.
UBS base case is two more Fed hikes, in December and March. Market pricing has fluctuated between three and four more hikes. Its Eurozone and UK hike views are also below market pricing.

The US 10-year yield fell toward 4.8% over the last month after a cycle high of 5.36% in early October. The catalyst was a risk-off move in equities and credit tied to AI capex financing. UBS expects the 10-year to settle in a 4.5-5% range.

October CPI came in hotter than expected after Governor Waller said the Fed should hike in December and was open to 50bp if inflation kept accelerating. Hike expectations and long-term rates went back over 5%, but the October highs were not retested.

UBS prefers the 2- to 5-year part of the Treasury curve, with a case for selectively extending toward the 10-year. It thinks hike expectations have moved too far too fast, beyond its 'recalibration hikes' base case.

UBS has growing conviction that the 10-year Bund yield peaked in late September. Yields above 3.5% tightened financial conditions, shown in wider French sovereign and high yield spreads. Eurozone growth is expected near 1% in 2027 and inflation to moderate, so UBS sees expectations of substantial ECB tightening as hard to realize.
Swiss inflation rose to 1.5% y/y in October, the highest since late 2023 and above SNB projections. UBS expects gradual SNB hikes in 2027, with about 60bp already priced over the coming year.

The Bank of England made its first hike of the cycle and gilt yields stabilized. Markets expect another hike in December and about 90bp more by end-2027. UBS sees best risk-reward in sterling high grade around the five-year point. The 28 October Budget was seen as uneventful.

Investment grade index spreads widened by mid-single digits over the past month. Hyperscaler bonds are about 4% of the US IG intermediate index, and most are rated AA or higher with debt capacity under current ratings.

High yield spreads widened about 70bp over three months to about 330bp in both the US and EU. The widening is concentrated in a few CCC credits. Trailing 12-month defaults are just under 2%, about half from liability management exercises. 60% of the universe is BB versus 40% ten years ago.
Refinancing needs next year are about 3% of the US and 8% of the EU high yield market, so there is no maturity wall. Weaker leveraged borrowers have mostly financed in loans and private credit.
The JP Morgan EMBI index rose 1.4% in October. UBS expects some EM spread tightening and cites stronger reserves, current accounts and fiscal positions plus lower corporate defaults.

Yields cited: investment grade about 6% in USD and 4.3% in EUR. High yield about 8.5% in USD and 6.8% in EUR, which UBS attributes to the repricing of policy rate expectations after the start of the US-Iran war.

sector_views.rationale: Attractive recommendation. Multidecade-high yields provide an income cushion and UBS sees yields stabilizing then falling gradually.
Attractive. Yields of 6% in USD and 4.3% in EUR, strong demand and solid fundamentals, with medium tenors preferred.
Attractive. Widening is largely idiosyncratic in CCC names, defaults are just under 2%, and low duration anchors returns. Higher-risk credit should stay short-dated.
Attractive. High carry, stronger fundamentals and a diversification benefit, with some spread tightening expected.

trade_ideas.description: Extend duration toward the 10-year area in quality issuers (Treasuries, Bunds, sterling high grade)
trade_ideas.rationale: Yields are at multidecade highs, and UBS expects hike pricing to prove too hawkish and yields to fall gradually next year.
trade_ideas.risk: Growth accelerates meaningfully and inflation keeps running hot.

trade_ideas.description: Own the 2- to 5-year segment of the Treasury curve as the best risk-reward
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS core view is that this segment offers the best risk-reward.
trade_ideas.risk: Hotter inflation prompting more Fed hikes than the base case.

trade_ideas.description: Keep higher-risk credit short-dated and hold stronger investment grade across medium tenors
trade_ideas.rationale: IG offers attractive carry, while higher-risk credit has idiosyncratic spread risk.

risk_factors: Growth accelerates meaningfully and inflation continues to run hot.
Hotter inflation could push the Fed beyond UBS's recalibration hikes.
Further repricing of AI-related credit, especially neocloud debt, and supply indigestion from hyperscaler issuance.
Lack of transparency on off-balance-sheet AI projects.
High energy prices eating into margins and savings.
High government debt and deficits limit fiscal support.
vol_and_positioning: Rate volatility reached a level that affected financial conditions, which UBS reads as a signal that the bond sell-off had gone too far.
Supply from US hyperscalers paused during 3Q earnings season and resumed after results. Strong IG demand and fund inflows have absorbed it.
geopolitical: The report attributes the repricing of central bank rate expectations and higher high yield yields to the start of the US-Iran war.
US midterm elections gave Democrats majorities in both houses, raising questions about AI regulation and continued data center buildout.
High government debt and deficits are political issues limiting further fiscal stimulus.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects only two more Fed hikes, below the three to four priced, with energy prices falling and financial conditions tightening, so yields should stabilize and then fall.
tension_points.bear_case: October CPI surprised to the upside, Governor Waller was open to a 50bp hike, and growth could accelerate while inflation runs hot.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth accelerating meaningfully while inflation continues to run hot, which UBS names as its risk scenario.

tension_points.bull_case: Compute demand is robust, most hyperscalers are rated AA or higher with debt capacity, and spreads may already price in excessive premia.
tension_points.bear_case: Neocloud spreads have repriced sharply, hyperscaler spreads imply multi-notch downgrades, and off-balance-sheet obligations lack transparency.
